description: Field vocabulary for extracting building-performance regulation facts (emissions factors, fuel coefficients, penalty rules, covered-building rules) from municipal PDFs. This is a vocabulary, not a data model — it defines what fields exist, their types, and how to extract them; grounding/lineage columns (source_chunk_id, extracted_quote, extraction_model, extracted_at) are added by the pipeline itself, not listed here. See datamodel.md for the corresponding Postgres tables.

EmissionsFactor.description: The allowed emissions intensity for one property type during one compliance period. Source: the property-type emissions-cap table found in the regulation text. Maps to: emissions_factors table.
EmissionsFactor.retrievalHint: table of greenhouse gas emissions factors by property type and compliance period

fields.description: The municipality this factor applies to (e.g. 'New York City', 'Boston'). Infer from the document's own text/letterhead — never assume it from the source filename or folder.

The exact property-type label as printed in the table (e.g. 'Multifamily Housing', 'Data Center'). Extract verbatim — this must join against a disclosure dataset's own property-type field, so do not normalize, abbreviate, or reword it.
First calendar year this factor applies to, inclusive. For a period printed as '2024-2029', this is 2024.
Last calendar year this factor applies to, inclusive. For a period printed as '2024-2029', this is 2029.

The numeric factor exactly as printed — do not round or convert. Preserve every significant digit shown (e.g. 0.000288962), since these coefficients are often precise to 6-9 decimal places and rounding changes downstream penalty calculations.
The unit exactly as printed (e.g. 'tCO2e/sf'). Do not assume a unit — municipalities may express this differently (e.g. per square meter instead of per square foot).

FuelCoefficient.description: The emissions coefficient for one fuel/energy type during one compliance period, used to convert a building's raw energy consumption into actual emissions. Source: the fuel-coefficient table found in the regulation text. Maps to: fuel_coefficients table.
FuelCoefficient.retrievalHint: table of greenhouse gas emissions coefficients by fuel type and compliance period

fields.description: The municipality this coefficient applies to. Infer from the document's own text, not the filename.

The exact fuel/energy source label as printed (e.g. 'Grid Electricity', 'Natural Gas', 'Fuel Oil #2', 'District Steam'). Extract verbatim — this must join against a disclosure dataset's own fuel-column naming, so do not normalize or abbreviate.
First calendar year this coefficient applies to, inclusive.
Last calendar year this coefficient applies to, inclusive.
The numeric coefficient exactly as printed — do not round or convert. Preserve every significant digit shown.

The unit exactly as printed. This varies by fuel type within the same table — e.g. electricity is commonly expressed per kWh while combustion fuels (gas, oil, steam) are commonly expressed per kBtu. Extract the unit shown for this specific fuel type; never assume it matches other rows in the same table.

PenaltyRule.description: A civil penalty provision for non-compliance: exceeding the emissions limit, failing to file a required report, or filing a false report. Source: statutory penalty language, typically prose rather than a table. Maps to: penalty_rules table.
PenaltyRule.retrievalHint: civil penalty for exceeding building emissions limit failure to file false statement

fields.description: The municipality this penalty applies to. Infer from the document's own text, not the filename.

Which non-compliance scenario this penalty covers. 'excess_emissions' = building filed but exceeded its emissions limit. 'late_filing' = building was required to report but did not (or filed late). 'false_reporting' = a filed report contained a knowing material false statement. Classify based on the provision's own language, not its section number.

First calendar year this penalty rate applies to, inclusive. Omit (null) if the statute does not scope this penalty to specific compliance periods — not every penalty provision changes by period the way emissions factors do.
Last calendar year this penalty rate applies to, inclusive. Omit (null) under the same condition as period_start.
The numeric penalty amount exactly as printed — e.g. 268 for a '$268 per ton' provision, or 500000 for a flat '$500,000' provision. No currency symbol or commas.

How the rate is applied, exactly as the provision states it — e.g. '$/tCO2e' for a per-ton excess-emissions rate, '$/sf/month' for a late-filing rate, or 'flat' for a single fixed amount like a false-reporting penalty.

Plain-English restatement of the calculation, only when the rate/rate_unit pair alone doesn't fully capture it. Explicitly note if the statute caps this as a maximum ('shall be liable for not more than...') rather than stating it as a fixed, guaranteed charge — that distinction matters for how downstream projections should treat the number.

CoveredBuildingRule.description: The criteria that determine whether a building is subject to this regulation at all — size thresholds and exemptions. Source: statutory 'covered building' definition, typically prose. Maps to: covered_building_rules table.
CoveredBuildingRule.retrievalHint: covered building definition gross square feet threshold exemption exception

fields.description: The municipality this rule applies to. Infer from the document's own text, not the filename.

'single_building' = the size threshold for one standalone building. 'multi_building_lot' = the combined threshold for multiple buildings sharing a tax lot. A jurisdiction typically states both as separate thresholds — extract each as its own row.
The gross square footage threshold at or above which a building/lot is covered, exactly as printed. No commas.
Plain-English description of how multiple buildings on the same tax lot get combined for the multi_building_lot threshold test. Omit for threshold_type = single_building.

Plain-English list of carve-outs or exemptions that remove an otherwise-covered building from this rule (e.g. affordable housing exemptions, non-profit healthcare adjustments, city-owned building phase-in schedules). One array entry per distinct exception — do not merge unrelated exceptions into one string. Summarize each in one concise sentence in your own words — do not quote the statutory text verbatim.
